doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: His father and the $21 for Tippin' In
summary: His father was a ragtime pianist who bought him his first good horn; he was paid $21 by RCA Victor for the hit Tippin' In.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yes. So that’s one of the ways. Now there are several other stories. I knew during those days that Louis Armstrong was very popular with the ladies you know. It’s easy to keep up with Satch’s age, because he was born in 1900. And frankly I wasn’t too far behind him, I was born in 1915, and my father was what we would call a ragtime piano player. As a matter of fact my father was the one who did the piano roll on “There’ll Be Some Changes Made.” And his name was Bobby Johnson. He had a lot to do with me, gave me my first horn, bought me my first good horn, a King trumpet, and he heard me play after I had joined Erskine Hawkins’ band, which I imagine you’ve heard, the million record seller we had was called “Tippin’ In.” And it’s still great. I got twenty-one dollars for it.
Twenty-one dollars from RCA Victor. Some friends of mine, lawyers and people have been trying to say that I should sue them. For what? I had, you know what I mean?
You had the pleasure of the music, anyway.
Yeah. I got a chance to do something that will be heard the rest of my life.
